scenario.description: Steady-state HotSpot 6.0 temperature of each layer of the proposed 3x3x3 TSV-based 3D-NoC versus a Monolithic 3D-NoC under synthetic benchmarks (Matrix, Hotspot 5%/10%, Uniform, Transpose). Router power comes from Synopsys PrimeTime energy per bit, scaled by traffic. The Monolithic maximum temperature is reported as 351.64 K (78.49 C), and the hottest TSV-based layer matches the coolest Monolithic layer. The paper publishes no router coordinates or per-router watts in text, so the case is not a complete reproducible experiment.
scenario.architecture: 3x3x3 3D Network-on-Chip with TSV-based inter-layer links (router floorplan Figure 2(c): 290 um x 290 um router, 220 um x 220 um logic), 45nm NANGATE library with FreePDK3D45 TSV, heat sink on top; compared with a Monolithic 3D design that has no bonding layers
scenario.workload: Synthetic traffic benchmarks (Matrix, Hotspot 5% and 10%, Uniform, Transpose) at maximum injection rate; no processing-element power
scenario.operating_point: 500 MHz, 1.1 V, maximum injection rate (saturation); steady-state temperature

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 6.0 steady-state grid thermal model (3D stack, with TSV-modified thermal resistivity per Table 3). Router power comes from Synopsys Design Compiler/ICC/PrimeTime energy per bit scaled by traffic flit counts (Eq. 3). PDF pp. 3-5, 8.
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper compares fixed layouts (Figure 2(b) vs 2(c)) and an optional four-corner thermal-TSV insertion; no automated floorplan or placement optimizer is used. PDF pp. 5, 9.
original_setup.controller: None. There is no thermal controller. DVFS is only a scaling equation (Eqs. 4-5), and the 500 MHz / 1.1 V operating point is fixed. Fluid cooling is mentioned as future work only. PDF pp. 5, 7, 11.
original_setup.benchmark: Synthetic traffic (Matrix, Hotspot 5%, Hotspot 10%, Uniform, Transpose) at maximum injection rate and 500 MHz on a 3x3x3 TSV-based 3D-NoC vs a Monolithic 3D-NoC (Figure 10, PDF p. 9). PARSEC via gem5 garnet 2.0 is a separate benchmark set. Router power: 7.64e-4 W static (Table 2; text on p. 7 gives 7.66e-4 W) and 9.2546e-13 J/bit (Table 2; text gives 9.246e-13).

thermal_observable.location: Hottest layer of the Monolithic 3D-NoC under the synthetic benchmarks (maximum temperature, stated as 78.49 C). Per-layer values appear only in Figure 10.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum steady-state HotSpot 6.0 grid temperature in the Monolithic 3D-NoC across the synthetic benchmarks. The text states the hottest TSV-based layer equals the coolest Monolithic layer; those values are not given numerically.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's system is a 3x3x3 3D stack with TSV and bonding-layer thermal resistivities and a heat sink on top, so it needs a layered 3D thermal model. A 2D single-layer or interposer-style Studio model cannot represent inter-layer heat flow, TSV conduction, bonding/TIM layers, or the per-layer temperature results in Figure 10.

The Monolithic vs TSV comparison depends on removing bonding layers and modifying TSV-area thermal resistivity (Table 3: Copper 0.0025 mK/W, TIM 0.25 mK/W, TSV area 0.0226 mK/W). These material and layer assumptions cannot be reproduced in a planar model.

The paper gives no router coordinates or per-router watts as text, since the per-router synthetic-benchmark powers are only in Figure 8. It publishes only router size, per-router static power and energy per bit, and traffic-scaled power charts. No complete same-scenario floorplan and power set exists.

The paper reports reliability (Black's model MTTF) as a primary outcome. The setup is not a controller or optimizer study, so there is no controller or optimizer to compare, and reliability calculations exceed a simple thermal setup.
The HotSpot 6.0 configuration (heat sink, package, convection, ambient, layer thicknesses) is not published in full, so the solver setup cannot be matched.

missing_inputs: No pinned packet assets were supplied (assets list is empty), so there are no config, floorplan or power files to inspect.
Router x/y placement coordinates for the 3x3x3 NoC, including TSV regions, are not published; only router size (290 um x 290 um) and logic size (220 um x 220 um) appear in Table 3.
Per-router power in watts for each synthetic benchmark is shown only in Figure 8 and is not given numerically; per-router powers would need digitizing with uncertainty.
The numeric per-layer temperatures of the TSV-based and Monolithic systems in Figure 10 are not published in text apart from the 351.64 K Monolithic maximum.
HotSpot 6.0 configuration details (layer thicknesses, heat sink, convection resistance, ambient temperature, grid resolution) are not given.
Die or stack dimensions, layer count geometry and silicon/bonding layer thicknesses are not given beyond the 3x3x3 architecture and Table 3 values.

Paper-linked URLs (Renesas and Toshiba handbooks, NanGate, FreePDK3D45, patent) are third-party references and do not provide inputs for this experiment; no code or data repository for this work is linked.
Exact traffic injection counts and execution times per benchmark are not published numerically.
